question: Should Dreaming localization become a stable memory-core config contract, and if so should it be a narrow language/locale hint, a custom template/prompt override, or both?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting a new persisted plugin config key or template override is a product/API choice with compatibility and safety tradeoffs that automation should not decide from this issue alone.

options.title: Consolidate On Canonical Design
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79223 as the product/API tracker and review one complete PR against that contract before merging localization support.

options.title: Accept Narrow Language Hint
options.body: Approve only a top-level `dreaming.language` or `dreaming.locale` key and ask contributors to drop template/prompt override behavior for now.

options.title: Defer Dreaming I18n
options.body: Keep English structural labels as the only supported runtime contract until maintainers prioritize broader localization work.

recommendation.title: Consolidate On Canonical Design
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79223 as the product/API tracker and review one complete PR against that contract before merging localization support.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Dreaming model override work changed the same public config, manifest, docs, and narrative surfaces that a localization contract would extend.
